title: Repository-native stateless phase pickup
summary: Evolve the bounded stage handoff to a closed repository-native v2 contract and add a pure stateless pickup coordinator. Normal Design, Plan, and Build completion and interrupted same-phase work publish deterministic handoffs whose repository artifacts, human authority, task scopes, acceptance proofs, and receipt lineage verify before any new-session effect.

current_state.summary: The repository already has three useful but disconnected capabilities: private ArtifactStore-backed stage-handoff/v1 and stage-startup/v1 for live runs; a legacy approved-shelf pickup with pickup receipts v1/v2 and repository-only resume; and BUILD-C checkpoint/integration for an already-authored exact scope. Normal phase completion does not publish a fresh-clone continuation artifact. The stage path depends on a workspace locator and RunStore, the legacy pickup is Build-only and starts at checkpoint rather than authoring, current pickup merge evidence contains host paths, and Design/Plan gate attribution is not yet exported as exact subject-bound repository evidence. The current Design lens wave also failed safely because its 16 dispatch entries omitted worker bootstrap and result-boundary fields.

alternatives.name: Repository-native stage handoff v2
alternatives.description: Add a closed taskplane.stage-handoff/v2 with repository-addressed artifacts and receipts, plus a stateless phase pickup coordinator. Keep the stateful loop as producer-side lifecycle authority, project true gate receipts at export, issue fresh attempt contracts after import, and enter the incumbent BUILD-C path only after scoped Build authoring.

gains: Reuses the existing stage, artifact, authority, checkpoint, and repository concepts without serializing private state
One schema covers requirement-to-Design, Design-to-Plan, Plan-to-Build, Build terminal evidence, and same-phase resume
Makes empty-home validation and pre-effect refusal mechanically testable
Preserves legacy pickup v1/v2 as a disjoint compatibility adapter
costs: Requires a new closed v2 schema and repository artifact store
Requires explicit producer adapters at Design, Plan, and Build completion
Requires a two-step Build pickup in which authoring precedes BUILD-C submission
tradeoffs.revisit_when: A remote artifact registry or cross-repository trust service becomes an approved product requirement; replace only the repository artifact resolver behind the same digest contract.

alternatives.name: Export and restore the current RunStore aggregate
alternatives.description: Serialize the current stage aggregate, private artifact store, locator, lifecycle receipts, and run metadata, then restore them in the successor before using the existing stage dispatcher.

gains: Reuses the current stage dispatcher without a new public projection
costs: Violates the explicit ban on run, locator, lease, and predecessor-runtime dependency
Turns mutable private lifecycle state into portable authority
Cannot prove fresh-clone and empty-private-home continuation
Leaks host-specific identities and creates replay ambiguity
tradeoffs.revisit_when: Never under R-0001; only a future requirement that explicitly makes private run migration the product could reconsider it.

alternatives.name: Stretch approved-shelf pickup v1/v2 across phases
alternatives.description: Add optional Design, Plan, phase, authority, and ordering fields to the existing approved-pickup contract and pickup receipt schemas and reuse the current tp.py pickup implementation.

gains: Reuses current source-trust and collision code
costs: Silently reinterprets closed v1/v2 contracts and refusal ordering
The one-element/one-criterion model cannot express Plan dependency order or same-phase progress
Current run_pickup begins at checkpoint and has no authoring contract
Would entangle compatibility logic with the successor authority model
tradeoffs.revisit_when: Only after the documented v1/v2 compatibility window ends and a separately approved migration permits a breaking legacy schema change.

decision: Use a repository-native stage-handoff/v2 and stateless phase coordinator because it is the only approach that preserves existing lifecycle and BUILD-C owners while making the sealed repository handoff the complete successor authority. The consumer remains a pure, synchronous, fail-closed boundary; the stateful loop may supply export material but no loop or private-store value survives into the handoff. Legacy pickup v1/v2 remains byte- and order-compatible on its existing command path.

contracts.description: Public repository-only export, pickup, submit, and same-phase resume surface with stable success and refusal envelopes.
Existing BUILD-C engine checkpoint and repository integration remain mandatory after scoped Build authoring.
Attributable initial, Design, and Plan gate receipts bind real human actors to exact subject fingerprints without synthetic authentication claims.
Add closed taskplane.stage-handoff/v2 and repository-artifact-reference/v1 while retaining private stage-handoff/v1.
Add phase-progress-receipt/v1 and complete predecessor chains while preserving pickup-receipt/v1 and v2 behavior.
Bounded phase startup with exact scoped view, full-envelope reference, attempt-local bootstrap, producer contract, lease, and closed result schema.
Path-free machine-readable outcome carrying boundary code, handoff/source identity, phase/mode, lineage, and verified checkpoint/integration status.

storage.publication: same-directory temporary, flush and fsync, no-follow validation, create-if-absent, exact-byte replay, same-identity conflict refusal

architecture.canonicalization: UTF-8 canonical JSON with lexicographically sorted object keys, compact separators, no NaN, schema-defined list order, and SHA-256 over every field except the top-level fingerprint
architecture.identity: handoff_id is SHA-256 of repository identity, source commit/tree, requirement fingerprint, producer phase/outcome, successor phase/mode, and predecessor handoff/receipt head; the canonical fingerprint covers the full manifest

phase_rules.terminal_rule: done may advance only to the declared next phase or terminal evidence; interrupted may resume only the same phase; a terminal predecessor is never reopened

authority_rules: Initial authorization is required for requirement-to-Design and is bound to the requirement fingerprint
Design approval is required for Design-to-Plan and Plan-to-Build and is bound to the current Design fingerprint
Plan approval is required for Plan-to-Build and is bound to the current Plan fingerprint
Actors must be explicit human:<identity> values; (unattributed), mechanical-definition-gate, missing, foreign, stale, mismatched, reused, or synthetic actors are refused
Mechanical progress receipts identify an engine producer and contain no human actor
cryptographic_authenticity_claimed remains false unless a separately verifiable public-key receipt is actually supplied
pre_effect_validation_order: input size, JSON, and closed schema
canonical fingerprint, list order, uniqueness, and bounds
repository identity, source commit/tree, tracked export lineage, and clean checkout
selected artifact existence, regular-file containment, bytes, and digest
progress/predecessor receipt chain, exact replay, and conflict
human authority subject, actor, source, freshness, and non-reuse
obligation partition, task dependency order, scope, contracts, acceptance, and proof closure

worker_dispatch.build_contract: write only the exact active Plan task scope; no dependency, contract, proof, or scope expansion
worker_dispatch.resume: issue a new attempt lease bound to the same handoff and receipt head; never import a predecessor lease or execution root

build_sequence: validate the complete Plan handoff and choose the first dependency-ready task
mint exact scoped authoring bootstrap, producer contract, lease, scoped view, result schema, and envelope reference
dispatch code authoring under the exact scope
validate the authoring result and exact Git diff before checkpoint calls
call the existing build_c.run_pickup checkpoint and repository integration boundary
validate and redact BUILD-C receipts into a path-free phase progress receipt
commit the progress receipt and expose only the next dependency-ready task

acceptance_map.criterion: AC1 Normal completion exports: completing Design, Plan, and Build through supported public flows produces one bounded sealed repository-resident handoff whose canonical fingerprint and repository-only artifacts verify after a fresh clone.
acceptance_map.design_element: One stage-handoff/v2 exporter is called by true Design, Plan, and final Build completion; it writes a 64-KiB closed manifest and digest-addressed artifacts under exports/pickup and records exact repository publication.
acceptance_map.validation: Parameterize Design, Plan, and Build completion, clone the resulting repository with an empty home, validate canonical bytes and all artifact digests, and assert exactly one handoff per phase identity.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC2 Fresh Design continuation: with only a clean fresh checkout, approved requirement/spec handoff, and empty private home, a new task starts Design with exact requirement identity, scope, contracts, and acceptance obligations while forbidden loop/run/track, lease, locator, conversation, and predecessor-runtime reads remain zero.
acceptance_map.design_element: Requirement-to-Design pickup validates the repository manifest and initial human authorization, then creates a fresh Design producer contract with design/** write authority and a full-envelope reference; private lifecycle modules are not consumer dependencies.
acceptance_map.validation: Run an isolated subprocess from a fresh clone and empty home with sentinels on every forbidden read, assert zero calls, and compare the emitted Design startup to the exact requirement, scope, contract, and acceptance bytes.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC3 Fresh Plan continuation: with only a clean fresh checkout, approved Design handoff, and empty private home, a new task starts Plan with matching source, requirement, Design fingerprint, contracts, and acceptance map; removed or stale Design approval is refused before dispatch.
acceptance_map.design_element: Design-to-Plan requires a current human Design approval receipt bound to the Design fingerprint and emits a Plan producer contract plus the exact acceptance map.
acceptance_map.validation: Exercise a fresh positive Plan pickup and sever the Design receipt, its actor, source, subject fingerprint, predecessor authority, and artifact bytes; every negative case must stop before dispatch.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC4 Fresh Build continuation: with only a clean fresh checkout, approved Plan handoff, and empty private home, a new task starts approved Build work in declared dependency order and exposes only exact task scopes, contracts, and proof commands; scope widening causes zero authoring and checkpoint calls.
acceptance_map.design_element: Plan-to-Build carries canonical ordinal tasks; the coordinator admits only the first dependency-ready task and mints an exact scoped authoring contract after comparing any request to sealed scope/contracts/proofs.
acceptance_map.validation: Use a multi-task dependency fixture, compare each dispatch byte-for-byte with the sealed task, then request a wider scope and assert authoring and checkpoint counters are both zero.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC5 Interrupted same-phase resume: after the first durable receipt, interrupted Design, Plan, and Build resume in a second checkout and empty private home, preserve completed obligations and exact predecessor digest lineage, schedule only remaining work, and never reopen a terminal predecessor.
acceptance_map.design_element: phase-progress-receipt/v1 forms an ordered predecessor digest chain; interrupted handoffs partition all obligations into completed and remaining and issue a fresh attempt lease only for remaining work.
acceptance_map.validation: Crash after the first durable receipt in each phase, clone the receipt commit, resume with an empty home, and prove no completed obligation is dispatched and done predecessors cannot be resumed.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC6 Complete closed lineage: every accepted successor artifact proves source commit and tree, repository, requirement, applicable Design and Plan fingerprints, producer phase and outcome, ordered task scopes/dependencies/contracts/acceptance proofs, authority, selected artifact digests, predecessor receipts, and canonical fingerprint; one-field omission, mutation, unknown-field, reorder, duplicate, and size-bound fixtures fail.
acceptance_map.design_element: The closed v2 manifest and closed nested schemas include every listed identity, bounded collection, canonical order, artifact digest, authority receipt, and predecessor head; no optional implicit lineage exists.
acceptance_map.validation: Generate one valid maximal fixture and mutate every field and nested field individually, plus reorder, duplicate, oversize, and digest cases; assert the stable structural or integrity refusal.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC7 Truthful authority: human identity and approval are attributable at real requirement, Design, and Plan gates, mechanical progress carries mechanical receipts, and missing, foreign, stale, mismatched, reused, or synthetic human authority is rejected.
acceptance_map.design_element: human-gate-receipt/v1 binds human:<identity>, context, exact gate subject, source/repository, decision and predecessor; phase-progress-receipt/v1 names only an engine producer and cannot claim a human actor.
acceptance_map.validation: Test valid initial/Design/Plan gate chains and a table of missing, foreign, stale, mismatched, reused, unattributed, mechanical-as-human, and synthetic actors before dispatch.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC8 Fail closed before effects: malformed, tampered, stale, foreign, ambiguous, dirty, incomplete, replay-conflicting, and scope-widened inputs each return a stable named refusal before dispatch, code authoring, checkpoint, publication, or integration, with every downstream effect counter remaining zero.
acceptance_map.design_element: One fixed validator order and stable refusal-code map precede attempt minting or all effect ports; export and pickup share collision, containment, and canonical validation.
acceptance_map.validation: Parameterize every named input class, instrument dispatch/authoring/checkpoint/publication/integration ports, and assert the expected boundary code, safe recovery, and five zero counters.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC9 BUILD-C is not bypassed: valid Build pickup receives exact scoped authoring, reaches existing BUILD-C checkpoint and repository-integration boundaries, and reports verified receipts; severing the pickup-to-BUILD-C edge or failing focused proof prevents completion.
acceptance_map.design_element: Build is explicitly authoring then submit; submit validates the authoring result and calls existing build_c.run_pickup, requiring engine checkpoint and repository evidence before minting a phase receipt.
acceptance_map.validation: Use real BUILD-C entry points in the positive CLI journey, remove the coordinator-to-BUILD-C callable, and fail the declared proof; only the positive journey may publish completion.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC10 v1/v2 compatibility: existing valid pickup v1/v2 shelf, trust-source, repository-only resume, collision, interrupted-write, and cold-start cases retain documented results and refusal ordering under unchanged legacy suites plus successor compatibility fixtures.
acceptance_map.design_element: The new public phase command and stage-handoff/v2 are schema-disjoint; taskplane/pickup.py, approved shelf schemas, pickup receipts v1/v2, --trust-source parsing, and legacy refusal order remain unchanged.
acceptance_map.validation: Run the unchanged legacy pickup and cold-start selectors beside a route-isolation fixture proving no successor file is interpreted as legacy or vice versa.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC11 No hidden-state dependency or leakage: every positive journey succeeds in a fresh clone and empty unrelated private home without loop.json, track, claim, lease, run store, locator, prior conversation, or predecessor runtime context; exports and public output contain none of those values, secrets, or absolute host paths.
acceptance_map.design_element: The consumer imports only pure repository/schema owners, selected blobs use digest locators, attempt values are new and ephemeral, exclusions are mandatory, and public receipts project out local repository paths.
acceptance_map.validation: Use forbidden-access sentinels and recursive serialized-content scans in fresh clones for every positive journey, then assert a clean checkout at the consumer preflight and zero hidden-state values or host paths.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC12 Deterministic public contract and recovery: identical semantic exports have identical fingerprints, exact replay is idempotent, same-identity byte conflicts fail closed, and every refusal names its boundary and safe recovery without weakening authority or widening scope.
acceptance_map.design_element: Canonical JSON, semantic handoff id, create-if-absent atomic publication, exact-byte replay, fixed refusal codes, and a closed recovery map make publication and consumption deterministic.
acceptance_map.validation: Export identical material in two clones, compare fingerprints and canonical bytes, replay exactly, inject a same-identity conflict and partial write, and assert stable boundary and safe recovery text.

risks.risk: A producer accidentally serializes private loop or host state into a portable artifact.
risks.mitigation: Closed schemas, mandatory exclusions, fixed digest artifact paths, forbidden-key/value scans, no-follow containment, and fresh-clone tests with private-state read sentinels.

risks.risk: Attribution is mistaken for cryptographic authentication or a mechanical step invents a human approval.
risks.mitigation: Require human:<identity> only from actual gate adapters, bind exact subjects and predecessor authority, record cryptographic_authenticity_claimed=false, and keep engine progress receipts actor-free.

risks.risk: A resumed Build widens scope or runs a task before its dependencies are green.
risks.mitigation: Compare the request to the sealed ordinal task, derive readiness only from verified predecessor receipts, mint the worker contract after validation, and verify the authored Git diff again before BUILD-C.

risks.risk: The successor path reports Build success without real BUILD-C proof.
risks.mitigation: Make build_c.run_pickup a mandatory post-authoring dependency, validate engine and repository receipts, and retain semantic severed-edge and failing-proof tests.

risks.risk: Atomic artifact publication leaves a collision, partial file, or unshareable working-tree-only result.
risks.mitigation: Use create-if-absent fsynced publication, exact-byte idempotency, conflict refusal, tracked-path verification, and repository-owner publication receipts; completion is not reported until the export commit is recorded.

risks.risk: A broad successor rewrite regresses legacy pickup v1/v2 refusal order.
risks.mitigation: Keep legacy pickup.py routing and schemas unchanged, place successor commands and schema in separate modules, and run existing suites unchanged in every slice.

risks.risk: The new modules work only in the repository and are omitted or fail on a supported Python runtime.
risks.mitigation: Verify clean-wheel contents/imports, direct and package import modes, strict typing, the Python 3.10 floor, and the Python 3.14 validation lane.

failure_modes.mode: Manifest JSON, schema, order, size, or fingerprint is invalid.
failure_modes.detection: Closed-schema and canonical-byte validation returns handoff-malformed or handoff-integrity before repository or effect ports.
failure_modes.recovery: Restore the exact repository artifact or re-export from the unchanged approved phase subject; do not ignore fields or recompute authority in the consumer.

failure_modes.mode: Repository, source commit/tree, or checkout cleanliness differs from the export.
failure_modes.detection: Repository identity and Git object verification returns repository-foreign, source-stale, or checkout-dirty.
failure_modes.recovery: Use a clean checkout of the recorded repository/export commit or create a new handoff from the new source; never trust-source around v2.

failure_modes.mode: A selected blob is missing, symlinked, untracked, oversized, or has different bytes.
failure_modes.detection: Repository artifact verification returns artifact-integrity before authority or dispatch.
failure_modes.recovery: Restore the exact digest-addressed blob from repository history or re-export the phase; never substitute another destination.

failure_modes.mode: A receipt chain has a gap, fork, duplicate, stale predecessor, or same-identity conflict.
failure_modes.detection: Ordered receipt validation returns receipt-lineage or publication-conflict.
failure_modes.recovery: Resume from the last single verified head or reconcile the interrupted atomic publication; do not choose between ambiguous forks.

failure_modes.mode: Required initial, Design, or Plan human authority is absent or does not bind the current subject.
failure_modes.detection: Authority validation returns authority-missing or authority-stale, including unattributed, synthetic, foreign, reused, or mismatched receipts.
failure_modes.recovery: Return to the real human gate for the exact current subject and export a new handoff; mechanical code cannot repair or invent approval.

failure_modes.mode: A same-phase handoff targets another phase or attempts to reopen a done predecessor.
failure_modes.recovery: Use next-phase pickup for done work or export interrupted work with an equal producer/successor phase.

failure_modes.mode: Requested Build scope, dependency order, contract, acceptance, or proof differs from the sealed Plan task.
failure_modes.detection: Task closure returns scope-widened, dependency-unmet, or proof-invalid before attempt bootstrap and authoring.
failure_modes.recovery: Use the exact sealed task or return to Plan and obtain a new attributed Plan approval; never widen in pickup.

failure_modes.mode: Authoring completes but BUILD-C checkpoint or repository integration does not verify.
failure_modes.detection: The submit path returns the existing BUILD-C/checkpoint/integration refusal and publishes no green progress receipt.
failure_modes.recovery: Correct the scoped implementation or focused proof under the same authorized task; if scope changes, return to Plan.

signals: phase export result: phase, outcome, source commit/tree, handoff fingerprint, artifact count/bytes, replay status, publication receipt fingerprint
phase pickup result: producer/successor phase, mode, receipt-chain head, completed/remaining counts, next eligible obligation, startup fingerprint
phase refusal result: stable boundary code, handoff/source identity when safely available, zero downstream-effect vector, and safe recovery code
Build submit result: authoring receipt fingerprint, BUILD-C checkpoint receipt digest, repository integration fingerprint, and progress receipt head
fresh-clone audit: forbidden hidden-state reads, serialized forbidden values, absolute host paths, private-home writes, and checkout cleanliness
observability.alerts_none_rationale: This is a synchronous local CLI and repository contract with no long-running service or SLO. CI is the actionable enforcement surface: any compatibility regression, nonzero hidden-state/effect counter, authority acceptance defect, artifact leak, or severed BUILD-C edge fails the exact selector and blocks delivery.

rollout.strategy: Deliver three independently reversible slices: (1) pure stage-handoff/v2 schema, canonical repository artifact publication, public manual export/pickup, and mutation fixtures; (2) Design/Plan/Build producer adapters, gate receipts, progress receipts, and same-phase resume; (3) normal loop completion wiring plus Build authoring-to-BUILD-C submit. Keep legacy pickup.py and receipt v1/v2 behavior unchanged throughout. Advance only when fresh-clone, zero-hidden-state, zero-pre-effect, authority, packaging, and existing legacy selectors are green.
rollout.rollback: Stop automatic v2 production at the single loop adapter and revert only the exact export publication commit or implementation slice. Retain already published v2 handoffs as immutable audit artifacts; older versions ignore their disjoint schema and no v1/v2 artifact is rewritten. If the v2 consumer is unavailable it fails closed as unsupported rather than falling back to legacy or private state.

rules: tp.py pickup <approved-design> remains the legacy entry and preserves all existing errors and ordering
tp.py phase handles v2 only; no auto-upgrade, permissive fallback, or trust-source flag is accepted
legacy repository-only receipt resume and interrupted-write reconciliation remain unchanged
v2 artifacts are ignored by legacy readers and are never downgraded into signed shelf authority
existing stage-handoff/v1 remains the private in-run representation and may be projected to v2 only by the validated public exporter

Use the recorded repository; do not override repository identity.
Checkout the recorded source/export lineage or create a newly approved handoff.
Preserve user work and retry in a clean checkout.
Restore every exact digest-addressed selected artifact.
Resume from the sole verified receipt head; do not choose an ambiguous fork.
Obtain the real required human gate decision for the exact subject.
Return to the real gate and export a new exact-subject handoff.
Use only the declared next phase or same-phase interrupted resume.
Use the sealed task scope or return to Plan for a new approval.
Complete and verify predecessor tasks in declared order.
Restore the exact sealed proof or return to Plan.
Preserve both candidates and reconcile to one exact approved identity; never overwrite.
